home-page.summary: An unofficial practice tool for the built-in mouse of CharaChorder 3D input devices. Train your cursor to arrive fast, and land right on target.

speed-mechanic.title: How the CharaChorder mouse speed works
speed-mechanic.fast: Move both 4-way joysticks in the same direction at once for Fast speed - use it to cover distance quickly.
speed-mechanic.slow: Move only one joystick for Slow speed - use it to fine-tune onto a precise point.
speed-mechanic.goal: This tool trains the switch between the two: a fast, coarse approach followed by a slow, accurate landing.

home-page.remark: Alnasl (pronunciation: /ælˈnæsl/) is the arrowhead star at the tip of Sagittarius's bow, marking where the arrow is aimed.

idle-hint.move: A target will appear. Move the pointer onto it and hold still until it fills in - no click needed.
idle-hint.click: A target will appear. Move the pointer onto it and click as fast and accurately as you can.
idle-hint.drag: A dashed circle marks the pickup point. Press down inside it, drag onto the solid target, then release.

description.move: Pure cursor movement: reach the target and hold still on it, no clicking.
description.click: Move then click: the standard point-and-click task.
description.drag: Press on the pickup point, drag onto the target, then release.

statistics-page.no-data-message: No practice sessions recorded yet. Finish a session on the Practice page to see your progress here.

information-page.description: This website, Alnasl, is an unofficial mouse practice tool designed for the built-in mouse of CharaChorder 3D input devices, including CharaChorder One, CharaChorder Two, CCU and Master Forge.

practice-page.title: practice page
description: At practice page, you can choose a mouse scenario (move, click, or drag) and difficulty (target count, size, and distance), then work through a round of targets arranged in a ring so every movement direction gets covered.
After each session you'll see your error rate, average movement time, and throughput (a Fitts's law measure of speed and accuracy combined).

statistics-page.title: statistics page
statistics-page.description: At statistics page, you can see your recorded practice sessions charted over time, split by mode, so you can track whether your throughput is improving.

settings-page.title: settings page
settings-page.description: At settings page, you can change the default practice mode and difficulty, switch the UI language, and clear your stored practice history.

description.0: Each trial's index of difficulty (ID) is calculated with the Shannon formulation of Fitts's law, where A is the distance travelled and W is the target size:
description.1: Throughput (TP) is the mean index of difficulty divided by the mean movement time, giving a single bits-per-second score that combines speed and accuracy - a higher number means you moved fast without giving up accuracy.
